When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

input.content:
# Bookshelf

A small reading list. No accounts, no database — books are stored in a JSON file.

```bash
npm start           # http://localhost:3000
npm test
```

- `PORT` — port to listen on (default `3000`)
- `BOOKS_FILE` — where to save books (default `data/books.json`, created on first add)

## How it works

Pages are rendered on the server and every action is a plain HTML form, so there
is no client-side JavaScript and no build step. It runs on Node's built-in
`http` module with no runtime dependencies.

Each book has its own URL (`/books/<id>`) that stands on its own, so you can
paste it to someone and they will see that book.

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /` | currently reading + finished, and the add form |
| `POST /books` | add a book |
| `GET /books/:id` | one book: title, author, notes |
| `POST /books/:id/finish` | mark finished |
| `POST /books/:id/notes` | save notes |

Writes go to a temp file and are then renamed over the real one, so an
interrupted write can't truncate your list. If the JSON file is ever
unparseable the app refuses to start rather than overwriting it.

## Files

```
server.js        starts the server
src/app.js       routing and request handling
src/store.js     the JSON file store
src/views.js     HTML rendering (all user input is escaped here)
test/            vitest suites for the store and the routes
```

content.text:
Done. `npm start` → http://localhost:3000.

**What it does**

- **Home** — "Currently reading" and "Finished" lists, plus the add form. Reading is newest-added first; finished is most-recently-finished first, with the date.
- **Add** — title, author, notes. Only the title is required; a blank one re-shows the form with an error and keeps what you typed.
- **Mark finished** — a button on the home list and on the book's own page. Records when.
- **Book page** — `/books/<id>` with title, author, added date, and notes you can edit and save.
- **Shareable links** — every book has its own URL that renders on its own from a cold GET, nothing client-side to hydrate. Paste it to anyone on the same host and they see that book.

**How it's built**

Server-rendered pages with plain HTML forms — no client-side JS, no build step, no runtime dependencies beyond Node's own `http`. Books go to `data/books.json` (override with `BOOKS_FILE`; `PORT` for the port).

Two things I did beyond the literal ask, both small: saves write to a temp file and rename over the real one so an interrupted write can't truncate your list, and if the JSON ever ends up unparseable the app refuses to start instead of overwriting it. All user text is escaped in one place (`src/views.js`), so a title like `<script>…</script>` renders as text.

Verified by running the actual app: added books, marked one finished, saved notes, restarted the process and confirmed everything came back from the file. 25 vitest tests cover the store and every route — `npm test`.

Two things I deliberately left out, since you said nothing fancy — say the word on either:

- **No un-finishing a book.** A mis-click currently means hand-editing the JSON. It's about a five-line toggle if you want the escape hatch.
- **No edit or delete for title/author.** Notes are editable; the rest isn't.

One note on sharing: this listens on localhost and has no accounts, so a link only works for someone who can reach the machine it's running on. Putting it somewhere a friend can load would need hosting — a separate decision, and worth a thought about whether you want your reading notes publicly readable.
